paragraphs.text: Now it came to pass, while the multitude pressed upon him and heard the word of God, that he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret;
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,
paragraphs.translit: Egeneto de en tō ton ochlon epikeisthai autō kai akouein ton logon tou theou kai autos ēn hestōs para tēn limnēn Gennēsaret,

paragraphs.text: and he saw two boats standing by the lake: but the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶδεν δύο πλοῖα ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiden dyo ploia hestōta para tēn limnēn, hoi de halieis apʼ autōn apobantes eplynon ta diktya.

paragraphs.text: And he entered into one of the boats, which was Simon`s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. And he sat down and taught the multitudes out of the boat.
paragraphs.original: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.
paragraphs.translit: embas de eis hen tōn ploiōn, ho ēn Simōnos, ērōtēsen auton apo tēs gēs epanagagein oligon, kathisas de ek tou ploiou edidasken tous ochlous.

paragraphs.text: And when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de epausato lalōn, eipen pros ton Simōna· Epanagage eis to bathos kai chalasate ta diktya hymōn eis agran.

paragraphs.text: And Simon answered and said, Master, we toiled all night, and took nothing: but at thy word I will let down the nets.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, διʼ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis Simōn eipen· Epistata, diʼ holēs nyktos kopiasantes ouden elabomen, epi de tō rhēmati sou chalasō ta diktya.

paragraphs.text: And when they had done this, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes; and their nets were breaking;
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai touto poiēsantes synekleisan plēthos ichthyōn poly, dierrēsseto de ta diktya autōn.

paragraphs.text: and they beckoned unto their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: kai kateneusan tois metochois en tō heterō ploiō tou elthontas syllabesthai autois· kai ēlthon, kai eplēsan amphotera ta ploia hōste bythizesthai auta.

paragraphs.text: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus` knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·
paragraphs.translit: idōn de Simōn Petros prosepesen tois gonasin Iēsou legōn· Exelthe apʼ emou, hoti anēr hamartōlos eimi, kyrie·

paragraphs.text: For he was amazed, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken;
paragraphs.original: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον,
paragraphs.translit: thambos gar perieschen auton kai pantas tous syn autō epi tē agra tōn ichthyōn hōn synelabon,

paragraphs.text: and so were also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs de kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn hyious Zebedaiou, hoi ēsan koinōnoi tō Simōni. kai eipen pros ton Simōna ho Iēsous· Mē phobou· apo tou nyn anthrōpous esē zōgrōn.

paragraphs.text: And when they had brought their boats to land, they left all, and followed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai katagagontes ta ploia epi tēn gēn aphentes panta ēkolouthēsan autō.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, while he was in one of the cities, behold, a man full of leprosy: and when he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en tō einai auton en mia tōn poleōn kai idou anēr plērēs lepras· kai idōn ton Iēsoun pesōn epi prosōpon edeēthē autou legōn· Kyrie, ean thelēs dynasai me katharisai.

paragraphs.text: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway the leprosy departed from him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekteinas tēn cheira hēpsato autou eipōn· Thelō, katharisthēti· kai eutheōs hē lepra apēlthen apʼ autou.

paragraphs.text: And he charged him to tell no man: but go thy way, and show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai autos parēngeilen autō mēdeni eipein, alla apelthōn deixon seauton tō hierei, kai prosenenke peri tou katharismou sou kathōs prosetaxen Mōysēs eis martyrion autois.

paragraphs.text: But so much the more went abroad the report concerning him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed of their infirmities.
paragraphs.original: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: diērcheto de mallon ho logos peri autou, kai synērchonto ochloi polloi akouein kai therapeuesthai apo tōn astheneiōn autōn·

paragraphs.text: But he withdrew himself in the deserts, and prayed.
paragraphs.original: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.
paragraphs.translit: autos de ēn hypochōrōn en tais erēmois kai proseuchomenos.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass on one of those days, that he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, who were come out of every village of Galilee and Judaea and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto en mia tōn hēmerōn kai autos ēn didaskōn, kai ēsan kathēmenoi Pharisaioi kai nomodidaskaloi hoi ēsan elēlythotes ek pasēs kōmēs tēs Galilaias kai Ioudaias kai Ierousalēm· kai dynamis kyriou ēn eis to iasthai auton.

paragraphs.text: And behold, men bring on a bed a man that was palsied: and they sought to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou andres pherontes epi klinēs anthrōpon hos ēn paralelymenos, kai ezētoun auton eisenenkein kai theinai enōpion autou.

paragraphs.text: And not finding by what [way] they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē heurontes poias eisenenkōsin auton dia ton ochlon anabantes epi to dōma dia tōn keramōn kathēkan auton syn tō klinidiō eis to meson emprosthen tou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And seeing their faith, he said, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn tēn pistin autōn eipen· Anthrōpe, apheōntai soi hai hamartiai sou.

paragraphs.text: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto dialogizesthai hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi legontes· Tis estin houtos hos lalei blasphēmias; tis dynatai hamartias apheinai ei mē monos ho theos;

paragraphs.text: But Jesus perceiving their reasonings, answered and said unto them, Why reason ye in your hearts?
paragraphs.original: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: epignous de ho Iēsous tous dialogismous autōn apokritheis eipen pros autous· Ti dialogizesthe en tais kardiais hymōn;

paragraphs.text: Which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise and walk?
paragraphs.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
paragraphs.translit: ti estin eukopōteron, eipein· Apheōntai soi hai hamartiai sou, ē eipein· Egeire kai peripatei;

paragraphs.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he said unto him that was palsied), I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go unto thy house.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: hina de eidēte hoti ho hyios tou anthrōpou exousian echei epi tēs gēs aphienai hamartias— eipen tō paralelymenō· Soi legō, egeire kai aras to klinidion sou poreuou eis ton oikon sou.

paragraphs.text: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφʼ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai parachrēma anastas enōpion autōn, aras ephʼ ho katekeito, apēlthen eis ton oikon autou doxazōn ton theon.

paragraphs.text: And amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God; and they were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to-day.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekstasis elaben hapantas kai edoxazon ton theon, kai eplēsthēsan phobou legontes hoti Eidomen paradoxa sēmeron.

paragraphs.text: And after these things he went forth, and beheld a publican, named Levi, sitting at the place of toll, and said unto him, Follow me.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai meta tauta exēlthen kai etheasato telōnēn onomati Leuin kathēmenon epi to telōnion, kai eipen autō· Akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: And he forsook all, and rose up and followed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai katalipōn panta anastas ēkolouthei autō.

paragraphs.text: And Levi made him a great feast in his house: and there was a great multitude of publicans and of others that were sitting at meat with them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετʼ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai epoiēsen dochēn megalēn Leuis autō en tē oikia autou· kai ēn ochlos polys telōnōn kai allōn hoi ēsan metʼ autōn katakeimenoi.

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with the publicans and sinners?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;
paragraphs.translit: kai egongyzon hoi Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis autōn pros tous mathētas autou legontes· Dia ti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiete kai pinete;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are in health have no need of a physician; but they that are sick.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho Iēsous eipen pros autous· Ou chreian echousin hoi hygiainontes iatrou alla hoi kakōs echontes·

paragraphs.text: I am not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.
paragraphs.original: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.
paragraphs.translit: ouk elēlytha kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous eis metanoian.

paragraphs.text: And they said unto him, The disciples of John fast often, and make supplications; likewise also the [disciples] of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de eipan pros auton· Hoi mathētai Iōannou nēsteuousin pykna kai deēseis poiountai, homoiōs kai hoi tōn Pharisaiōn, hoi de soi esthiousin kai pinousin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, Can ye make the sons of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen pros autous· Mē dynasthe tous hyious tou nymphōnos en hō ho nymphios metʼ autōn estin poiēsai nēsteusai;

paragraphs.text: But the days will come; and when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, then will they fast in those days.
paragraphs.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
paragraphs.translit: eleusontai de hēmerai, kai hotan aparthē apʼ autōn ho nymphios tote nēsteusousin en ekeinais tais hēmerais.

paragraphs.text: And he spake also a parable unto them: No man rendeth a piece from a new garment and putteth it upon an old garment; else he will rend the new, and also the piece from the new will not agree with the old.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elegen de kai parabolēn pros autous hoti Oudeis epiblēma apo himatiou kainou schisas epiballei epi himation palaion· ei de mēge, kai to kainon schisei kai tō palaiō ou symphōnēsei to epiblēma to apo tou kainou.

paragraphs.text: And no man putteth new wine into old wine-skins; else the new wine will burst the skins, and itself will be spilled, and the skins will perish.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·
paragraphs.translit: kai oudeis ballei oinon neon eis askous palaious· ei de mēge, rhēxei ho oinos ho neos tous askous, kai autos ekchythēsetai kai hoi askoi apolountai·

paragraphs.text: But new wine must be put into fresh wine-skins.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον.
paragraphs.translit: alla oinon neon eis askous kainous blēteon.

paragraphs.text: And no man having drunk old [wine] desireth new; for he saith, The old is good.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai oudeis piōn palaion thelei neon· legei gar· Ho palaios chrēstos estin.
